[LNAM.2.5.1] **Mixed-script — reject.** An identifier must satisfy UAX #39 **Highly
Restrictive**: it must be single-script, or use one of the recognized augmented sets
(Latin + Han + Hiragana + Katakana; Latin + Han + Bopomofo; Latin + Han + Hangul),
with script-neutral characters (digits, `_`) permitted throughout. The compiler must
reject an identifier that violates this. A conforming compiler may implement Highly
Restrictive **conservatively**: over-rejecting a multi-script identifier that a full
UAX #39 per-character set-cover would admit is permitted (it errs toward the
security-safe direction), but it must never *admit* a mixed-script identifier Highly
Restrictive forbids. Full set-cover is a v1.x refinement (D-B1-1). *(This admits legitimate CJK, which mixes
Han and kana, and blocks Latin/Cyrillic homoglyph names such as `pаypal`. It is the
whole script-security surface: DS carries no cross-identifier confusable-skeleton
lint.)*
